name: Tapo P110 (EU)

radios.note: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi only. TP-Link says Bluetooth is used to speed up setup.

matter.note: No official source states Matter support or explicitly rules it out for the P110; product pages simply don't list it. TP-Link's Matter version is the separate Tapo P110M.

apple_home.note: TP-Link's P110 pages list Alexa, Google Assistant and SmartThings and don't mention Apple Home, but no official page says it is unsupported. The Tapo P110M is the Matter version.

google_home.note: Through the Tapo cloud link (Works with Google Home). Set the plug up in the Tapo app first.

alexa.note: Through the Tapo Alexa skill, linked to your TP-Link account.

smartthings.note: Through the Tapo partner integration in the SmartThings app, signed in with your TP-Link ID.

home_assistant.note: Home Assistant's TP-Link Smart Home integration lists the P110 among supported Tapo plugs. Newer devices need your TP-Link account credentials once.

hubRequired.note: Wi-Fi plug that joins your 2.4 GHz router directly and is set up in the Tapo app; no bridge is listed.

localControl.note: Home Assistant's TP-Link integration controls it over the local network, though newer firmware needs TP-Link account credentials to authenticate. We found no TP-Link page on Tapo-app control without internet.

energyMonitoring.note: Real-time and historical energy use in the Tapo app, with bill estimates from your electricity rate.

maxLoadWatts.note: 16 A / 3680 W for general use and resistive loads. TP-Link's load FAQ says EV chargers are not supported on Tapo/Kasa plugs.

summary: The EU Tapo P110 is a 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi plug rated 16 A / 3680 W that tracks energy use in the Tapo app. TP-Link lists Alexa, Google Assistant and SmartThings, all through account linking, and Home Assistant supports it through its TP-Link integration. TP-Link doesn't list Apple Home or Matter for it; the separate Tapo P110M is the Matter version.
caveats: TP-Link doesn't list Apple Home or Matter for the P110. If you need Apple Home, the Tapo P110M is the Matter version.
Energy readings show in the Tapo app; TP-Link's SmartThings article says advanced features such as energy data stay in the Tapo or Kasa app.
Home Assistant's TP-Link integration asks for your TP-Link account credentials once on newer firmware.
Not for EV chargers: TP-Link's load FAQ says their charging current can exceed the plug's rating.
